steps.body: One whole can be split into 10 equal parts. Each part is called one tenth of the whole.
steps.narration: One whole can be split into 10 equal parts. Each part is called one tenth of the whole.

widget.prompt: Shade the strip to show 0.3. Each column is one tenth.

commonCounts.feedback: The count of shaded columns must match the tenths digit of 0.3 — that digit is 3, so 3 columns.

widget.successFeedback: Exactly 3 of the 10 columns — 3 tenths, which the decimal writes as 0.3.
widget.lowFeedback: The shaded amount is still below the target. Each column is one tenth — count the shaded columns against the decimal.
widget.highFeedback: The shaded amount has gone past the target. Each column is one tenth — count the shaded columns against the decimal.

predict.prompt: The strip has 10 equal columns and you will shade 3 of them. How much of the whole strip is that?
predict.reveal: Each column is one of 10 equal parts — one tenth. Shading 3 columns covers 3 tenths of the whole, which the decimal 0.3 names.

widget.prompt: A unit square is split into 10 equal columns, and 3 of them are shaded. Write the shaded amount as a decimal.

commonErrors.feedback: That is the count of shaded columns, and a count of parts is a whole number. Each column is one tenth of the square, so 3 columns is 3 tenths, written with the 3 in the tenths place.
That puts the 3 in the hundredths place, which would mean 3 cells of a hundred-cell grid. This square has only 10 columns, so each shaded column is a tenth of the whole.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Each column is one tenth of the square. Count the shaded columns and write that count in the tenths place, directly after the decimal point.

explanationVariants: The 4 sits in the tenths place, so the fraction is 4/10.

widget.prompt: Which fraction names the same amount as 0.4?

options.feedback: Correct — the digit 4 sits in the tenths place, so 0.4 means 4 of 10 equal parts.
A denominator of 100 would mean 4 hundredths, written 0.04. The digit 4 in 0.4 sits one place higher — in the tenths place.
That fraction has the part count and the number of equal pieces swapped. The decimal names 4 pieces out of 10 equal pieces, so 4 belongs on top.
A denominator of 1 would make this 4 whole units. The decimal point in 0.4 says the amount is less than one whole, cut into 10 equal parts.
